ratings_why.fun: The curve climbs well: borrow to tier fast early, Warden and Thought in the middle, then a real late choice between holding debt (Seven, Eldest) and clearing it (Corbie); Joy and Silver-Spoon are the flat spots.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7 because the Ledger makes debt a visible resource whose interest is fuel, so hold-or-clear is a new decision each turn that no tribe today asks; the pawnshop replay adds a second fresh engine.

verdict_why: The tiers do their jobs and the hot spots are already named in risks; more rounds would change cards, not improve the shape.

points.text: Grandmother Corbie plus Uncle Jack pawning a junk unit each turn is a cheap clear every turn: about 2 gold for +3/+3 to every Syndicate unit, doubled by Memory. That is a good capstone loop; let the owner see it in a sim before touching it.
Sorrow can hand a Tier 3 player a Tier 6 copy after one loss, which skips the tier curve. A cap of your tier +1 keeps the comeback without breaking pacing; worth trying if sims show it swings.
Joy only pays its neighbours and needs clears, so it is weak away from Sorrow. Letting it give the +1/+1 to every unit touching Joy would make the pair a real mid-game buffer.
Gallows Lane Enforcer does not say what protection does when you owe nothing. A line like the Bagman's ('if you owe nothing, gain 1 gold instead') would read cleanly and keep it useful.

Seven makes holding a full Ledger free, which removes the cost of the hold path late. That is fine as a capstone, but it means the hold build has no late tension; the owner may want Seven to pay only up to 3 interest.

standouts.why: Uncle Jack turns selling into a loan and a replay of When-played text; it opens a build no other tribe has.
Grandmother Corbie is a capstone the comp is built to reach, and it pulls against Corbie's Eldest.
Mr Magpie is a strong early body whose price is the tribe's first slip, so turn one already teaches the Ledger.

weakest.why: Joy needs a clear and the right neighbours to do anything, and gives little when it does.
The Silver-Spoon Magpie is a generic counter-pick that does not touch the Ledger.
Oast Clerk caps at +2/+2 a turn, a small seed that stops growing before the late game.

flags.note: Golden Memory with golden Corbie and five clears a turn is about +60/+60 per Syndicate unit a turn; a real high roll, worth the two-pass runaway check.
Pawn plus the Bagman's Skim brings a unit home free after every win, netting gold and a replay each turn; it needs wins, so losing is the counterplay.
The Mirror at Tier 4 can become a second Grandmother Corbie or Seven, doubling a capstone a tier early.
Tier 6 copies offered at Tier 3 after a loss can skip the tier curve.
No rule for protection when you have no IOU.
